Dead game, if you don't have any friends to play with, do not buy it.

Sad, because it's an ok game, devs are cool too, but it's the way she goes.

I love this game.   Its a lot of fun and terrific with some friends.  I know its had its criticism calling it a L4D clone, but the game play mechanic that it is using its pure fun and it feels more refined than Left 4 Dead. The funky Retro-Future vibe of the art direction is terrific and really plays into my love of that genre of sci-fi.  This is one of the best games for jumping into and blowing off some "steam" by shooting endless rounds of alien invaders.  It never feels like the same game twice due to the director Ai, that scales the challenge to your own game play skills.  The game is still considered early access, and under development. I love how responsive the devs are to ideas and implementing changes and bug fixes.  Some software companies should take notice here (I'm looking at you Autodesk!)  Amazing work being done by a world class Indie Studio! Watch out for the Flasher!
Awesome game....left 4 dead vibes, can't wait until they finish it!

I really recommend this game with friends and on intense difficulty, if you play this game solo with bots it's super boring because the game's director goes wayyy easier on you if you have 3 bots wich makes the game feel very boring i almost refunded it at first because of that but then i played with 2 friends and it was a completely different experience the game is extremely fun has a decent variety of weapons, the aesthetic is really good i just hope this game can actually get a good playerbase because right now it's only me and my friends worldwide who plays it so that's why i don't recommend playing it without friends because you probably won't find randoms to play with if you didn't bring friends with you, it's a very underrated game deffinitly shouldn't be with how nice the gameplay feels and the level design is great

It could have potential, but it's not there yet.

Despite not having much playtime, I could tell within the first 10 minutes of gameplay that this game would not be fun, even with friends.

The gunplay and feedback are unsatisfying. Explosions have no depth or power. The enemies are boring. The map design is lacklustre, with poor signposting towards your current objective.

I may revisit this in the future. But, for now, it's been refunded.

There are only two words that I can describe this game with: terrible and underwhelming.

For how long this game has been around, there is absolutely no reason for it to be this bad. It completely and totally fails to be anything more than extremely pale imitation of a L4D-esque game. 

The game is devoid of interesting content, or basically any content at all. The level design is terrible and un-intuitive, the world is boring and empty, and the atmosphere is non-existent. 

The game controls and functions poorly, the gunplay stinks, and the main gameplay loop is dull. Even the sound is underwhelming and completely lacking impact. The AI director is bad, the AI is bad, and the hordes are underwhelming. 

Did I mention the game also runs poorly? Outside of it clearly being an unoptimised mess, I had constant issues with either getting kicked, my friend getting kicked, or one of us crashing.  

The Anacrusis could basically be summated as "L4D without any of the things that made it good (and also much worse)". 

This is one of the few games I've refunded, and the only game I've ever purchased to date that makes me feel like I got ripped off, even at 50% off.

Maybe you guys should've put the same amount of effort into actually making the game good that you did making the hundred billion funny barrel meme achievements.

[hr][/hr]
[b]Edit:[/b] Credit where credit is due, the devs have appeared to fix the connectivity issues in Update 36, but regardless, this game is in a sorry state.

[hr][/hr]
[b]2024 Edit:[/b] The devs are now gaslighting people about the player count. It's just sad and reads like denial, copium, or both.

reviews.review:
This game can be extremely fun and overall does has potential, however 1.0 barely done anything to improve the game from early access and the devs are now 'too uncomfortable' to take feedback now.

Alot of people say they're were disappointed with B4B because it was marketing heavily off of the L4D series. I say that exactly what The Anacrusis is doing and barely getting any players

I really wish Steam had a "mixed" option, but generally I feel I have more negative things to say than positive, so I'll mark it as such.

The Anacrusis is yet-another co-op horde shooter, as copying Valve's iconic Left-4-Dead seems to be a growing trend all of a sudden. Set in a retro-futuristic 1970's themed spaceship, the crew appears to have been overtaken by facehugger-like alien parasites (or is it a viral/bacterial infection, and their heads are just mutated to look alien? It's not clear, which is a running problem here.) You fight your way through hordes of these afflicted crewmembers with laser-based weaponry, and make your way to safety.

You have your usual tropes you'd expect; 4 "characters" (more on this later), linear maps that end in a saferoom, you have your "special" enemies like a slime-based enemy that can encase survivors in a slime or create puddles that slow you down, a ranged grabber enemy that's sorta like the Smoker from L4D, and naturally the brute-like tank that soaks up damage and is designed to break up the pace and require the team work together to focus fire on it and take it down. There's a few new ideas, such as these "perk" stations that let you upgrade your character (much, much, much better executed than B4B's card system).

Gunplay is "serviceable"; guns feel okay to shoot, but it pales in comparison to L4D2's incredible gore and destruction. Enemies splatter with this glowing orange blood, which does almost feel like a "censored" option, or something like the "cartoon gore" option in Serious Sam games. (This blood also doesn't seem to appear on the enemy's model or on the environment, but I may be misremembering.) Upon death, they don't have the incredible variety of mo-cap death animations that seamlessly blend into a ragdoll that L4D has; they just kinda "flop over dead" into ragdoll instantly which feels a bit silly and lacks impact or weight. Overall it's not exactly a super high-budget game, and it does kinda show in the basic gunplay.

However, the single biggest issue with this game, is unfortunately the lack of immersion or detailing. 

The characters are very basic; they seem to just have basic reactions like "Oh look an enemy!" or "Oh look a shop I used to go to!" without any real commentary or personal input. The characters all feel like the same cardboard cutout; compare this to the diverse cast of it's inspiration, L4D. You have Bill, the grisled Vietnam veteran who's living on borrowed time, and serves as an almost jaded father-figure to the group with a heart of gold. Louis, the optimistic office worker who always tries to keep the group in high spirits. Francis, the meatheaded biker who jokingly hates everything and has a weird and entertaining sense of humor. And finally Zoey, the college student who has a bit of a perky attitude and keeps her team in check, mostly. L4D2 goes even further! You have Coach, the wholesome small-town PE coach who has a similar role to Bill but with a lot more optimism and lightheartedness. Ellis, the lovingly immature gun-toting redneck who's always telling tall-tales about his friend we never meet. Nick, the somewhat self-absorbed conman who at first hates his team (particularly Ellis) but over time learns to get along and even enjoy their company. And finally you have Rochelle, who is...uh...well the one "non-character" I think Valve has ever made. She just kinda has very basic reactions to everything, and doesn't really have anything personal or unique to interject ontop of it. 

The Anacrusis characters all feel like clones of Rochelle. That's about all you need to know about them tbh.

The environments are visually very interesting in terms of artstyle, but there doesn't seem to be nearly as much character as the ironically more mundane settings of it's inspiration. It's kinda just a ship, with maybe a few cool ideas (such as that large garden-like atrium full of fake plants with a massive screen overhead simulating a fake sky, with some damaged/glitching panels exposing the illusion) but overall it's mostly just "hallways and rooms". L4D did a lot with selling the feeling of a viral/bacterial outbreak, and how survivors and the military response might've played out, with plenty of environmental storytelling, bodybags and quarantine posters all around, and all sorts of small details that help the world feel varied and lived-in. In the Anacrusis; for example, weapons just kinda appear in this kind of weird "default pose" in the middle of a hallway or room without much rhyme or reason. (Even just putting a body, a trail of blood, some dead aliens nearby, and positioning the gun to look like it fell out of their arms as they died would go miles to improve this.) You don't really feel like an outbreak happened here beyond the random bits of damage to the ship (why is this room utterly destroyed? what happened here? No explanation seems to be implied or given; it just is. Meanwhile in L4D campaigns, you'd have at least some dead bodies or items nearby to imply that maybe survivors tried blowing their way through a wall in a tough spot but it backfired, if not directly seeing the cause yourself, such as the insanely memorable plane crash sequence in the Dead Air campaign.)

And finally, the little details. The soundtrack and sound design, is, forgettable honestly. L4D had amazing tracks that sold the tension and atmosphere, and tons of little music cues for when ambient zombies were still around, when the player was at high stress, low stress, when special zombies spawned or were attacking you, etc. The guns firing, the various special zombie screams, the sound of a crying witch somewhere in the area, it all came together and made an unforgettable sound experience. The Anacrusis has a selection of combat tracks that play during specific events in a campaign, and that seems to be just about it. And of those very few tracks, they're all so honestly generic and forgettable I'm struggling to remember a time I was fighting back zombies and just having a blast with the music, like I would have all the time in L4D.

Overall, as another negative review puts it, "The Anacrusis is L4D but without the stuff that made L4D memorable."

Going from L4D to The Anacrusis, it's like getting a delicious steak at a restaurant. You want to have it again at home, so you buy the same exact cut of steak at the store. You expect it to have the same flavor and taste because hey it's the same cut; it has all the core features of that delicious steak, right? But with that first bite, you're saddened to find out it misses the magic; it wasn't cooked the same way, it didn't have the same seasonings and care for small details, and you're eating it in your studio apartment instead of the carefully crafted fine-dining atmosphere of the restaurant you were just at. It ticks all the big boxes, but brushes aside all the little ones that make an otherwise "average" game great. 

It's really, really rough around the edges, but there's still a good strong backbone there. They just need to build the rest of the animal around it.
Left4Dead in space without everything that makes L4D fun

It's Left 4 Dead in space with aliens as zombies, they're constantly improving the game, and they're adding a versus mode. What more could you ask for?

The Anacrusis is a game I wanted to like but, very much like Back 4 Blood, touts itself as a spiritual replacement for Left 4 Dead ... but just isn't. 

Allow me to explain what they got right first:
The environment of the spaceship is rather nice. It looks bright, colorful, clean, with the right retro-futurist stylings to make it feel like it used a 1960's lens to imagine what spaceships would look like. The "sets" look like they were borrowed from the original Start Trek, Space 1999, or Logan's Run. Even the characters ooze with that great golden era of color TV sci-fi vibe. They absolutely nailed this. 

The other thing they get right is the minimalist controls needed to play, 4 cardinal movement keys, jump, crouch, flashlight, use, and a mouse to handle rotation, inventory, and shooting .... that's it. That's all you need. For a casual shoot that is nearly perfect.
-------

However, looking great and having the right vibe does not make for a good game, just a pretty one. And here is where Anacrusis drops the ball. The Anacrusis makes an attempt to replicate the casual co-op environment that Left 4 Dead mastered but didn't learn the lessons L4D teaches on "how" to be an amazing co-op. 

The major issue, as I see it, is that Anacrusis is more of a close quarters combat horde shooter in game play, When you look at L4D, Back 4 Blood, or Zombie Army, you have expansive maps where the pacing of the horde events makes them feel organic to game play. Maps in Anacrusis are "tight" and these hordes occur primarily in hallways or small rooms. There's no feeling like you can prepare or work cooperatively to defend your positions ... just suddenly there's dozens of aliens in every direction swarming the party and the cooperative element falls away into a chaos of enemies everywhere. It instantly devolves into an every man for themselves twitch and spam shooter. Go play L4D's "No Mercy" and you'll absolutely see perfection in a co-op shooter in terms of pacing, environment, and tension.

Related to what I consider the environmental issue above are the enemies themselves, most specifically the specials. When your team is being swarmed by dozens of standard aliens constantly during a horde event it takes away from the tension the specials should be adding to the game. Brutes just zip around beating people up (like that wasn't already happening) or people are getting glued or grabbed and the specials feel more like an annoyance than a dangerous monster that must be dealt with. And it is because the hordes are just chaotic events solely designed to swamp the player that the specials lose that "sting" ... there's so much going on that they don't feel dangerous or special, just something else that needs to be spammed with a few left-clicks.

Environment, pacing, and enemy behavior - those are the three top issues with this title that prevents it from reaching it's goal of being a "Left 4 Dead style casual co-op". In it's current state it is a spam shooter that leaves out much of the co-op elements needed for replayability. In fact, at this time, the lobby system is broken and you can't even play with friends which entirely breaks what this game was supposed to be... a casual, fun, team co-op game. It does look nice but, you know, for being 14 years old L4D still looks good and it delivers on all of those promises.

The Anacrusis and Back 4 Blood both have a lot in common. They’re both trying to be as good as Left 4 Dead and they’re both made by indie teams. However, there is one big difference between the two: The Anacrusis team still has time to back out.

Imagine this sisyphean task: a small, inexperienced group is asked to re-create and then make a few twists on a highly successful AAA game series by one of the best developers in the world. 
They have to recreate the gunplay, the sound design, the music, the enemy AI, the character models, the game balancing, the good UI, and all the subtleties that a professional studio like Valve has the time and (arguably infinite) money to create. 

Along the way, this indie team has to find funding and stay motivated while having their work scrutinized against professionals in their field. It’s an unfair task no one should accept. And yet here we are, with two different indie teams that have given themselves this impossible goal.
For Stray Bombay though, there’s still hope. 

Unlike Turtle Rock’s Back 4 Blood, The Anacrusis has three important words on its Steam store page: [b]Early Access Game[/b]. At this stage in development, with more than 30 updates already put in, I would not blame Stray Bombay if they decided to stop development and move on to a project that will not be compared against a game by one of the greatest game companies of all time. This team clearly has talent, just not enough experience or money yet to take on the gargantuan task of what Anacrusis wants to be. 

I’ll continue to follow along with the development of The Anacrusis, but I’m more interested in what Stray Bombay’s next project might be.

This is a great game to play with friends! I look forward to experiencing the full game when it releases!
